Normal.description: Normal skin is generally balanced, comfortable, and not excessively oily or dry. It can still experience occasional sensitivity, dehydration, or sun damage.
causes: Consistent, gentle skincare and sun protection
Genetic factors and a stable skin barrier
symptoms: Little dryness, flaking, or excess oil
dos: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen every morning
Moisturize regularly and maintain a consistent routine
donts: Do not use harsh products when the skin feels comfortable

night: Optional gentle treatment based on individual concerns

prevention: Use sunscreen daily and reapply when outdoors
Avoid smoking and keep a balanced diet
Patch-test new products and avoid unnecessary product changes
Normal.severity: Usually low severity when the skin is comfortable and free of persistent symptoms.
Normal.when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a dermatologist for persistent irritation, new or changing lesions, unusual pain, or changes that do not improve with gentle care.

Acne.description: Acne is a common inflammatory skin condition caused by blocked pores, excess oil, bacteria, and inflammation. It can affect people of any age.
causes: Excess oil production and blocked hair follicles
Hormonal changes, including puberty and menstrual cycles
Inflammation, certain medicines, and products that clog pores
symptoms: Red bumps, pustules, or tender deeper spots
Post-acne dark marks or scars in some people
dos: Wash gently twice daily and after heavy sweating
Introduce one acne treatment at a time and use it consistently
donts: Do not squeeze, pick, or scratch spots
Do not scrub aggressively or use many irritating treatments together
Do not stop treatment after only a few days if there is no irritation

morning: Optional salicylic acid product if tolerated
night: A thin layer of an appropriate acne treatment, such as adapalene or benzoyl peroxide

prevention: Keep hands, phones, and frequently touched surfaces clean
Use products labeled non-comedogenic and avoid picking lesions
Acne.severity: Severity ranges from occasional mild comedones to extensive, painful, or scarring acne.
Acne.when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a dermatologist for painful deep acne, scarring, widespread breakouts, significant distress, or acne that does not improve after about 8 to 12 weeks of consistent care. Seek medical advice before using retinoids during pregnancy.

Wrinkles.description: Wrinkles are lines and folds that become more visible as skin loses collagen, elastin, and moisture over time. They are a normal part of skin aging.
causes: Natural aging and reduced collagen and elastin
Ultraviolet radiation, smoking, pollution, and dry skin
symptoms: Fine lines around the eyes, forehead, or mouth
Deeper folds or creases over time
dos: Moisturize to support skin comfort and reduce the appearance of dryness
Introduce active ingredients gradually and follow product directions
donts: Do not use tanning beds or intentionally tan
Do not combine multiple strong anti-aging products without checking for irritation

night: Retinoid on selected nights if appropriate and tolerated

prevention: Use sunscreen, protective clothing, and shade
Avoid smoking and maintain adequate hydration
Sleep well and use gentle products that do not chronically irritate the skin
Wrinkles.severity: Usually low medical severity, although rapid or unusual skin changes should be assessed.
Wrinkles.when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a dermatologist for personalized anti-aging treatment, sudden changes, persistent irritation, or any spot that bleeds, changes, or does not heal.

Eczema.description: Eczema, often called atopic dermatitis, causes itchy, dry, and inflamed skin. It can flare when the skin barrier is weakened or exposed to triggers.
causes: A weakened skin barrier and inherited tendency
Irritants such as fragrances, harsh cleansers, and detergents
Allergens, dry weather, heat, stress, or infections
symptoms: Dry, itchy, scaly, or cracked skin
Red, darker, or inflamed patches depending on skin tone
Oozing, crusting, or thickened skin during some flares
dos: Apply a fragrance-free moisturizer frequently, especially after bathing
Use lukewarm water and gentle fragrance-free cleansers
Keep nails short and identify personal triggers
donts: Do not scratch or use rough scrubs on affected skin
Do not use fragranced products or very hot water
Do not apply prescription steroid treatment without following medical guidance
recommended_ingredients: Hyaluronic acid in a fragrance-free formula

morning: Rinse or use a gentle fragrance-free cleanser
Use sunscreen suitable for sensitive skin if tolerated
night: Apply moisturizer while skin is still slightly damp
Use any prescribed treatment exactly as directed

prevention: Use fragrance-free laundry and skincare products
Protect skin from cold, dry air and known irritants
Eczema.severity: Severity can range from mild dryness and itching to extensive, painful, or infected flares.
Eczema.when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a doctor for persistent or severe eczema, sleep-disrupting itch, spreading rash, signs of infection such as pus or fever, or symptoms near the eyes.

Rosacea.description: Rosacea is a long-term condition that commonly causes facial flushing, persistent redness, visible small blood vessels, and sometimes acne-like bumps.
causes: A tendency toward facial blood-vessel reactivity and inflammation
Sun exposure, heat, hot drinks, alcohol, spicy foods, or stress in some people
symptoms: Frequent flushing or persistent central facial redness
Small visible blood vessels or acne-like bumps
Burning, stinging, dryness, or irritated eyes
dos: Use gentle fragrance-free products and mineral sunscreen
donts: Do not use abrasive scrubs, astringents, or fragranced products
Do not expose the face to excessive heat or unprotected sun
Do not self-treat persistent redness with strong steroid creams
recommended_ingredients: Niacinamide at a low concentration if tolerated
Mineral sunscreen with zinc oxide or titanium dioxide
prevention: Wear a hat and seek shade in strong sunlight
Keep a trigger diary and manage heat and stress where possible
Patch-test products and introduce changes gradually
Rosacea.severity: Severity varies from occasional flushing to persistent redness, bumps, eye symptoms, or thickened skin.
Rosacea.when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a dermatologist for persistent or worsening redness, eye pain or vision changes, frequent flares, or thickening of the skin. Eye pain or vision changes need prompt medical attention.

Dark Spots.description: Dark spots are areas of increased skin pigment, often called hyperpigmentation. They can follow inflammation, sun exposure, hormonal changes, or injury.
causes: Marks left after acne, eczema, or other inflammation
Hormonal changes, some medicines, or skin injury
symptoms: Flat brown, gray, or darker patches
Uneven skin tone in areas exposed to sun or previous inflammation
Spots that may darken after irritation or sun exposure
dos: Use broad-spectrum sunscreen daily and reapply outdoors
Introduce brightening ingredients slowly and stop if irritation occurs
donts: Do not pick at acne, bites, or rashes
Do not use unregulated bleaching products or household remedies
Do not over-exfoliate or skip sunscreen

morning: Vitamin C or niacinamide if tolerated
night: Azelaic acid or another dermatologist-recommended treatment

prevention: Use sunscreen and protective clothing consistently
Control acne, eczema, and other sources of inflammation
Avoid picking and patch-test new products
Dark Spots.severity: Usually low medical severity, but the cause should be checked if spots are new, changing, or unusual.
Dark Spots.when_to_consult_doctor: Consult a dermatologist for rapidly changing, irregular, bleeding, painful, or non-healing spots, or for pigmentation that does not improve after several months of gentle care.
